rows.rule: check 1 (no report within +/-12 h); check 4 (spike looks real)
rows.evidence: No Harris County STEERS report of any type was running within +/-12 h. Two hours over the trigger (15.84, then 12.09 ppb after midnight) with 1,3-butadiene up at the same hour (4.37 ppb vs 0.04 baseline); no flag next to the spike.

rows.rule: check 1 (only report far off the wind); check 4 (three hours over trigger)
rows.evidence: One report running within +/-12 h: a maintenance activity 23.9 km away, 100 deg off the wind, listing neither compound. Spike holds for three hours (10.02, 14.84, 12.06 ppb).

rows.rule: check 4 (spike starts on the first valid hour after a calibration check)
rows.evidence: No report within +/-12 h, so no report was missed. But the spike starts on the first valid hour after the analyzer's span (ST) and blank (BL) hours, and at this site in 2024 hours right after a flagged hour read >= 10 ppb 2.8% of the time (10/351) vs 0.6% (30/5097) otherwise. A second hour is also over (11.05 ppb), which argues for a real reading. Would decide it: TCEQ's final validated AutoGC data (these are provisional) or the site's span-check log for that night.

rows.rule: check 1 (report outside even the 45 deg wedge); check 3 (placement differs, same outcome)
rows.evidence: One report within +/-12 h, starting 1.2 h after the spike hour; it lists benzene and unspeciated VOCs, no 1,3-butadiene. By its street address it sits 5.9 km away, 63 deg off the wind; the pipeline's name match put it at a same-name site 9.5 km away, 49 deg off. Outside the 45 deg wedge either way. Single hour over (13.96 ppb) after hours of 2-5 ppb.

rows.rule: check 1 and 2 (lumped-VOC report outside the 45 deg wedge, started after the spike)
rows.evidence: Two reports within +/-12 h. One is 20.1 km away, 118 deg off the wind, neither compound. The other lists only lumped VOC (563 lb), sits 14.4 km away 63 deg off the wind, and started 0.9 h after the spike hour, while air at 3.6 mph needs ~2.5 h to cover 14.4 km. Wind is borrowed from Milby Park (no wind at this site). Spike: two hours over, 1,3-butadiene up too.

rows.evidence: No report of any type running within +/-12 h. Rising over three hours (9.97, 14.40, then 7.14 ppb after midnight); no flag next to the spike.

rows.rule: check 1 and 2 (lumped-VOC report outside the 45 deg wedge in every nearby hour)
rows.evidence: One report within +/-12 h, running for 26 days, listing C4 hydrocarbons and a lumped 'VOC - nonmethane' line but no 1,3-butadiene; 8.8 km away at bearing 79 deg, 54 deg off the detection-hour wind. The wind at this monitor from 19:00 to 02:00 CST came from 133-210 deg, never near 79 deg. Spike barely over the trigger (10.78 ppb) for one hour, 3.03 ppb next.

rows.rule: check 1 (report inside the 45 deg wedge, not the 22.5 deg corridor)
rows.evidence: A flaring report was running at the spike hour, 11.3 km away and 38 deg off the wind: inside the wider 45 deg wedge, outside the pipeline's 22.5 deg corridor. It lists sulfur dioxide, CO, H2S and light hydrocarbons, no benzene and no lumped VOC line. The wind is borrowed from Milby Park 3.8 km away (no wind at this site) and turned from 142 to 181 deg over the next hour. Would decide it: wind measured at Galena Park, or a speciated flare analysis for that event.
